climate.overview_html: Carbon Brief’s September 2026 state-of-climate analysis places 2026 on track to be the second-warmest year on record (~1.51°C above pre-industrial), with median Niño 3.4 forecast at +3.1°C peak and a 35% probability — a near-doubling over four months — that 2026 sets a new global temperature record; 2027 is projected at ~1.7°C and is the year most at risk of comfortably exceeding the record. A new Nature Geoscience paper (23 September) by Witte, Zappa and McGillis demonstrates that rain-induced dilution of surface-ocean carbonate chemistry intensifies global CO2 uptake by ~13.6% relative to wind-only estimates — implying current carbon budget models underestimate the ocean sink by 10 ± 5%, a correction that would partially offset land-use emissions accounting in global inventories. The UNGA week of 22–27 September was dominated by national net-zero announcements and renewed attention to the UNEP “Limiting Overshoot” framing — context for Germany’s fossil-fuel roadmap, the WMO Seasonal Update and the Super El Niño autumn outlook already covered this week.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of the Climate September 2026: Strong El Niño Puts 2026 on Track for Second-Warmest Year (~1.51°C); 35% Probability New Global Record; 2027 Projected ~1.7°C; Niño 3.4 Median Forecast +3.1°C Peak; More Than 91% of Model Runs Predict Strongest Modern-Record Event
items.summary: Carbon Brief's September 2026 state-of-climate analysis updates the global temperature outlook in the context of the ongoing Super El Niño. The first six months of 2026 ranked as the third-warmest start to any year on record at approximately 1.4°C above pre-industrial levels. The probability that 2026 sets a new global temperature record has nearly doubled over four months to 35%, with the central estimate placing 2026 at approximately 1.51°C above pre-industrial levels as the second-warmest year. More than 91% of ensemble model runs predict the current El Niño will be the strongest in the modern instrumental record, with median Niño 3.4 peak near +3.1°C. The analysis flags 2027 as the year most at risk of a new record (~1.7°C), as the lagged atmospheric and SST response to peak El Niño conditions amplifies global mean temperature well into the following calendar year.

items.headline: Rain-Induced Dilution Intensifies Global Ocean CO<sub>2</sub> Uptake by ~13.6%; Current Global Carbon Budget Models Underestimate Ocean Sink by 10 ± 5%; Two-Thirds of Effect via Freshening-Induced Carbonate Repartitioning; Published in Nature Geoscience
items.summary: A global analysis published in Nature Geoscience quantifies the effect of rainfall on air-sea CO2 exchange. Rain reduces surface salinity and shifts carbonate equilibrium toward higher CO2 solubility, both locally diluting dissolved inorganic carbon and altering the partial-pressure gradient driving gas exchange. The study derives a total rain-induced increase in ocean CO2 uptake of approximately 13.6% above wind-only estimates; freshening-induced repartitioning of the carbonate system accounts for roughly two-thirds of this effect. Carbon budget models that do not incorporate rain effects underestimate the ocean carbon sink by an estimated 10 ± 5%. If confirmed at inventory scale, upward revision of published ocean sink estimates would partially reduce the implied terrestrial-biosphere contribution to the atmospheric CO2 balance. Changes in global precipitation patterns under continued warming will also alter future ocean carbon uptake capacity.

weather.overview_html: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae) has passed south of Okinawa and intensified to 185 km/h as it steered past the Daito Islands toward Japan’s mainland; significant wind and rain impacts are forecast for the Tōkai and Kantō regions by late Wednesday–Thursday, before extratropical transition on October 3. In the Central Pacific, Hurricane Nolo remains Category 4 at 145 mph / 945 hPa as of 0300 UTC September 29, now ~430 miles WSW of Honolulu and moving northwest, with gradual weakening expected to begin tonight — sparing the main Hawaiian Islands a direct landfall but sustaining Papahanaumokuakea under a hurricane watch. The 2026 Oregon wildfire season has become one of the worst on record: 1,873 fires have burned 2.54 million acres including the 578,637-acre BIG GRASS Fire still at 94% containment, with elevated fire-weather conditions persisting in Northern California through September 29.

items.headline: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae / JTWC 25W) UPDATED September 29: Intensified to 185 km/h After Passing South of Okinawa; 393 km ENE Kadena Air Base; Tracking East-Northeastward South of Honshu; Potential Tōkai/Kantō Approach Late Wednesday–Thursday as Severe Tropical Storm; Extratropical Transition October 3; Airline Advisories Tokyo/Nagoya Pending
items.summary: Typhoon Queenie (Surigae, JTWC 25W) has moved northeast through and past the Daito Islands, intensifying to approximately 185 km/h maximum sustained winds as of September 29, up from 150 km/h at its closest approach to Okinawa. The centre is now located 393 km east-northeast of Kadena Air Base, tracking east-northeastward at 20 km/h. Steady weakening is forecast to commence as the storm encounters increasing vertical wind shear and cooler sea surface temperatures south of Honshu. JTWC guidance projects the system will track east-northeast south of Honshu before its closest approach to the Izu Islands and the Tōkai and Kantō coastal regions around late Wednesday–Thursday, October 1–2, by which point intensity is expected to have weakened to severe tropical storm level. Extratropical transition is forecast October 3. The Japan Meteorological Agency has noted the 2026 western Pacific season has produced the highest September cyclone count since 1966. Airline advisory updates for Tokyo Narita, Haneda and Nagoya Chūbu are expected from major carriers as the storm's track and timing become clearer.

items.headline: Hurricane Nolo Central Pacific UPDATED September 29 0300 UTC: Category 4 at 145 mph / 945 hPa; ~430 Miles WSW Honolulu; Moving NW at 11 kt; Gradual Weakening Begins Tuesday Night; Hurricane Watch Active Papahanaumokuakea; Main Hawaiian Islands Spared Direct Landfall
items.summary: As of 0300 UTC September 29, Hurricane Nolo is centered near 18.8°N 163.7°W, approximately 430 miles west-southwest of Honolulu, maintaining Category 4 intensity with maximum sustained winds of 145 mph and a minimum central pressure of 945 hPa. The storm is moving northwest at 11 knots. NHC advises that a gradual weakening trend is expected to begin Tuesday night, followed by accelerating weakening mid-week as Nolo encounters increasingly unfavorable sea surface temperatures and wind shear. Dangerous conditions are expected within the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument starting Tuesday. The northwest track continues to keep the storm well west and southwest of the main Hawaiian Islands; the Big Island continues to receive elevated rainfall and surf. Nolo's persistence at Category 4 makes it the longest-lasting major hurricane of the 2026 Central Pacific season.

items.headline: 2026 Oregon Wildfire Season: 1,873 Fires / 2.54 Million Acres as of September 22; BIG GRASS Fire 578,637 Acres at 94% Containment; Rowe Creek Complex 373,927 Acres at 99%; Season Surpasses 2020 Oregon Record; Elevated Fire-Weather Northern California Through September 29; Super El Niño Drought a Key Driver
items.summary: The 2026 Oregon wildfire season has burned 2,543,011 acres across 1,873 fires as of September 22, exceeding the 2020 Oregon season total and ranking among the worst on record. Two deaths have been attributed to the season. The largest single fire, the BIG GRASS Fire in Malheur County, has burned 578,637 acres and was at 94% containment as of September 11. Other major fires include the Rowe Creek Complex (373,927 acres, 99%), Coleman Creek Fire (308,863 acres, 100%), Henry Fire (229,844 acres, 99%) and Hay Creek Complex (200,292 acres, 100%). Residual fire-weather risk continues in Northern California through September 29, with daytime relative humidity 10–25% and wind gusts to 30–40 mph over the Sierra Nevada. The severe season reflects Super El Niño-driven precipitation deficits across the Pacific Northwest during the 2025–2026 winter and spring, combined with record-low spring snowpack across the Sierra and Cascades; NIFC's seasonal outlook maintains above-normal fire potential through October in Northern California.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s headline transaction is ESR Group’s agreement to acquire 100% of Aquila Clean Energy APAC from Aquila Group, adding a 1.6 GW portfolio spanning solar, battery storage and wind across Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan — explicitly to supply clean power to ESR’s regional data-centre and logistics tenants. In Europe, Lirion Power acquired a 77 MW Irish wind portfolio targeting life extensions, repowering and solar-plus-storage hybridisation at existing grid connections, while Poland’s PAD RES Group secured approximately $50 million in long-term financing for three solar projects totalling 133 MW in southwestern Poland. The Super El Niño context also raises shorter-term operational risk: Typhoon Queenie’s proximity to the Izu Channel offshore wind corridor introduces curtailment risk for assets in the Izu and Kii Channels through early October.

items.headline: ESR Group to Acquire 100% of Aquila Clean Energy APAC: 1.6 GW Solar, Battery Storage and Wind Portfolio Across Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan; Explicitly Targets ESR Data-Centre Power Supply; Transaction Expected Close Q1 2027
items.summary: ESR Group, one of Asia-Pacific's largest listed real-asset managers, announced on September 25, 2026 an agreement to acquire 100% of Aquila Clean Energy APAC from Hamburg-based Aquila Group. Aquila Clean Energy APAC operates a 1.6 GW portfolio of operational, under-construction and advanced-development solar PV, battery energy storage and wind assets across Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan. Financial terms were not disclosed; close is expected in Q1 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. ESR's strategic rationale centres on directly integrating renewable generation into its regional logistics-real-estate and data-centre platform to supply contracted clean power to hyperscale tenants. PV Tech notes ESR already has active solar and battery storage pipelines in several APAC markets, and the acquisition substantially accelerates that build-out. The deal is characterised as the largest single clean-energy platform acquisition in Asia-Pacific by portfolio capacity in 2026.

items.headline: Lirion Power Acquires 77 MW Irish Wind Portfolio; Plans Life Extensions, Repowering and Solar-Plus-Storage Hybridisation at Existing Grid-Connected Sites
items.summary: Lirion Power acquired a 77 MW portfolio of operating wind farms in Ireland with plans to increase asset value through operating-life extensions, repowering and hybridisation with solar generation and battery storage at existing grid-connected locations. Irish wind assets with established grid connections carry significant scarcity value in 2026 given the constrained grid queue, making portfolio acquisitions of this type an increasingly common route to accelerated renewable capacity growth without the multi-year interconnection wait.

items.headline: PAD RES Group Secures ~$50 Million Long-Term Financing for 133 MW Polish Solar Portfolio: Krapkowice 90 MW, Strzelce Opolskie 18 MW and Gromadka 25 MW in Southwestern Poland
items.summary: Polish renewable-energy developer PAD RES Group secured approximately $50 million in long-term project financing covering three solar projects totalling 133 MW in southwestern Poland: the 90 MW Krapkowice project, the 18 MW Strzelce Opolskie project and the 25 MW Gromadka project. Poland added approximately 4.5 GW of solar in 2025, driven by government support mechanisms and EU Green Deal co-financing. PAD RES positions the deal as part of a broader Central European solar expansion strategy.

science.overview_html: Microsoft Research posted MW-Nowcast (arXiv:2609.34836, September 28) — a six-hour ensemble radar nowcasting model that doubles available warning time for extreme precipitation by matching the skill of three-hour methods out to six hours across independent data from the US, Europe and China. In a formal GRL publication, Landsberg and Barnes (GRL, published 24 September) show that AI weather and climate models produce boreal winter land temperature forecasts systematically cold by an amount equivalent to 15–20 years of recent warming — a training-data cutoff problem that is strongest at the hottest extremes and affects both medium-range weather models (FourCastNet, Pangu) and long-range climate emulators. Separately, Deutscher Wetterdienst published the technical description of AICON, an icosahedral graph-neural-network forecast model at 13 km resolution trained on ICON-DREAM reanalysis and in full operational use at DWD since 1 March 2026 — making DWD the first national meteorological service outside ECMWF to run a fully data-driven global model as an operational 24/7 product alongside its physics-based suite. Also newly in print, the Nature Geoscience study on rain-induced CO2 flux intensification (September 23) is directly relevant to ocean-carbon modelling applied to climate projection.

items.headline: MW-Nowcast (arXiv:2609.34836): Microsoft Six-Hour Ensemble Radar Nowcasting of Extreme Precipitation; Doubles Warning Time vs. State-of-the-Art; Higher Detection Skill than Leading Generative Baselines for Heavy and Extreme Rainfall Across US, Europe and China; Pretrained Checkpoint Publicly Released
items.summary: MW-Nowcast is a six-hour ensemble radar nowcasting model that jointly trains a deterministic predictor to capture organized precipitation structure shared across ensemble members and a generative component producing diverse local residuals around this shared prediction. Evaluated across independent datasets from the United States, Europe and China, MW-Nowcast achieves higher detection skill than leading generative methods for heavy and extreme precipitation throughout the full six-hour horizon. For the most intense rainfall events, MW-Nowcast doubles the available warning time — delivering six-hour forecasts with skill previously limited to three hours for the leading generative baseline. A cost-loss decision analysis confirms the model retains substantial value for a broad range of decision-making applications at 4–6 hours, where alternative methods offer little benefit. The pretrained checkpoint was released publicly alongside the paper. Extended nowcasting horizons have direct operational relevance for municipal flood emergency management, aviation weather avoidance, hydroelectric reservoir operations and transportation network management.

items.headline: Landsberg & Barnes GRL (10.1029/2025GL119740): AI Weather and Climate Models Cold-Biased by Equivalent of 15–20 Years of Warming; FourCastNet and Pangu Forecasts of 2020–2025 Boreal Winter Temperatures Resemble ERA5 from 2000–2010; Bias Strongest at Hottest Extremes; Same Defect in Climate Emulators
items.meta: Jacob B. Landsberg & Elizabeth A. Barnes · Geophysical Research Letters · e2025GL119740 · Published 24 September 2026
items.summary: Landsberg and Barnes diagnose a systematic cold bias in the boreal winter land temperature distributions produced by leading AI weather and climate models: FourCastNet and Pangu produce 2020–2025 forecasts of observed temperatures that are too cold relative to ERA5, with the deficiency equivalent to the warming accumulated over the past 15–20 years — the model's implicit temperature reference resembles the climate of the early-to-mid 2000s rather than the current decade. The cold bias is strongest at the hottest extremes of the temperature distribution, suggesting limited training exposure to the most recent episodes of record heat. The same structural defect is found in long-period climate emulators trained on historical ERA5 and used for future projection. The study uses ERA5 itself as the comparison standard, meaning the documented bias is a lower bound on real-world error because ERA5 itself carries a slight cold bias relative to surface observations. The finding directly reinforces the need for periodic model retraining on updated reanalysis and has immediate implications for energy-sector forecasting during the current Super El Niño and record global temperatures.

items.headline: AICON (arXiv:2608.24651): DWD’s Icosahedral GNN Global Forecast Model at 13 km Trained on ICON-DREAM; First National Met Service Outside ECMWF to Run Fully Data-Driven Global ML Model Operationally; In 24/7 Operational Use at DWD Since 1 March 2026; Competitive Skill vs. Physics-Based ICON Especially Near-Surface Variables
items.meta: Deutscher Wetterdienst team · arXiv:2608.24651 [physics.ao-ph] · Submitted 25 August 2026
items.summary: AICON is an operational global machine learning weather forecasting model developed by Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) generating forecasts at 13 km spatial resolution with 3-hour time steps. The architecture employs a Graph Neural Network with encoder-processor-decoder structure and graph attention mechanisms, operating on an icosahedral multi-mesh derived from ICON's native grid and trained exclusively on the high-resolution non-hydrostatic ICON-DREAM reanalysis. A key design choice is to avoid autoregressive multi-step rollout during training, prioritising small-scale fidelity at short-to-medium forecast horizons. Routine operational verification against surface and upper-air observations shows skill competitive with the physics-based ICON model, particularly for near-surface variables (2-m temperature, 10-m wind, surface pressure). AICON entered full 24/7 operational status at DWD on March 1, 2026 and runs alongside the physics-based suite — making DWD the first national meteorological service outside ECMWF to support a data-driven global model as a live operational product. This represents a milestone in the institutional adoption of ML forecast systems beyond the research context.

items.headline: Rain-Induced Dilution Intensifies Global Ocean CO<sub>2</sub> Uptake by ~13.6%; Current Carbon Budget Models Underestimate Ocean Sink by 10 ± 5%; Freshening-Induced Carbonate Repartitioning Accounts for Two-Thirds of Effect; Published in Nature Geoscience 23 September
items.meta: Carson R. Witte, Christopher J. Zappa, Wade R. McGillis · Nature Geoscience · Published 23 September 2026
items.summary: A global analysis by Witte, Zappa and McGillis quantifies the effect of rainfall on air-sea CO2 exchange using a global framework that accounts for both local dilution and freshening-induced repartitioning of the carbonate system. Rain reduces surface salinity, shifting carbonate equilibrium toward higher CO2 solubility and amplifying the partial-pressure gradient driving gas exchange. Total rain-induced ocean CO2 uptake is estimated at approximately 13.6% above wind-only calculations, with carbonate-system repartitioning accounting for roughly two-thirds of the total effect. Current global carbon budget models that exclude rain-effect parameterisation underestimate the ocean carbon sink by approximately 10 ± 5%. The finding implies that future changes in global precipitation patterns under continued warming will alter ocean carbon uptake capacity in ways not currently captured by standard Earth system models, and that the diagnosed underestimate needs to be factored into revised global emission-budget calculations.

items.title: Fortune / PitchBook September 23: Climate-Specialist VC Fundraising Down ~40% YoY While H1 2026 Climate-Tech Deals Up 55% to $26 Billion; AI and Data-Centre Energy Demand Driving Divergence; Growth-Stage Surges 78%; Seed Falls 20%; Earth Observation Funding Tripled
items.body_html: PitchBook data cited by Fortune on September 23 show that fundraising for climate-specialist venture capital funds fell nearly 40% year-on-year in 2025, continuing the decline from peak years 2021–2023 — a pattern Fortune attributes to limited partner fatigue with long hold periods and uneven exit performance in climate hardware. However, the deal landscape itself is more complex: CTVC’s H1 2026 tracker shows total climate-tech startup funding reached $26 billion in January–June 2026 — up 55% year-on-year — with low-carbon data centres, earth-observation data platforms and grid-infrastructure software capturing the bulk of incremental capital. Growth-stage investment surged 78% while seed-round counts fell 20% and Series A deal counts dropped 22%, indicating capital concentration in proven later-stage companies. Earth-observation startups tripled their intake as AI model operators sought real-time geospatial and historical training data. The Fortune analysis notes that AI is simultaneously a headwind (data-centre energy demand competing with decarbonisation budgets) and a tailwind (AI-optimised grid forecasting, energy management and climate-risk analytics platforms attracting new allocators) for climate-tech investing, creating a fundamentally two-speed market between infrastructure-adjacent growth plays and pure climate-hardware bets.

items.title: ESR Group to Acquire Aquila Clean Energy APAC: Largest Single Clean-Energy Platform Acquisition in Asia-Pacific by Capacity in 2026; 1.6 GW Across Five Markets; Hyperscale Data-Centre Power Demand the Strategic Driver
items.body_html: ESR Group announced on September 25 an agreement to acquire 100% of Aquila Clean Energy APAC from Hamburg-based Aquila Group, adding a 1.6 GW portfolio spanning solar, battery storage and wind assets across Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan and Taiwan. PV Tech notes the deal is strategically distinct from typical renewables consolidation: ESR’s explicit motivation is to directly supply contracted clean power to hyperscale data-centre and logistics-real-estate tenants in Asia-Pacific — a model that integrates generation assets into real-estate investment platforms rather than treating them as standalone energy infrastructure. Energy Storage News describes the deal as the largest single clean-energy platform acquisition in Asia-Pacific by portfolio capacity in 2026 and a signal of accelerating consolidation among regional renewable developers as hyperscale demand drives structural need for contracted clean-power supply chains. Transaction value was not disclosed; close is expected in Q1 2027 subject to regulatory approvals.
